changes: p1: name normalized to 'Vācaspati' (miśra moved to titles only, per stem-form rule)
p2: name normalized to 'Yadolāla Ratnākara' (the ms reading 'yadolālala' looks like dittography; the catalogue gives Yādolāla); confidence lowered to medium
date.tithi: 'gauha' is not a corruption. It is the vṛddhi derivative of Guha (the day sacred to Guha/Skanda = ṣaṣṭhī, 6). The Āryā metre needs the long 'gau'
date.weekday: 'saume' read as Monday (sauma < soma); Wednesday (saumya) is possible but less likely
date: chronogram verified (arvan 7, abdhi 4, adri 7, indu 1, read right to left = 1747); added a note on current vs. expired year
purpose normalized to 'svārtha (for the scribe's own use)'

notes: The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram: arvan (horse) 7, abdhi 4, adri 7, indu 1. Read right to left this gives Śaka 1747, which is ŚS+78 = 1825 CE. The colophon is a single Āryā verse. 'Gauha' (gau long) is metrically required and means 'belonging to Guha', i.e. ṣaṣṭhī. The scribe's name: the ms has 'yadolālala'. The metre (27 mātrās) works with either 'yadolālala' or the catalogue's 'yādolāla', so the name is probably Yādolāla/Yadulāla with a doubled 'la'. 'Ratnākara' is probably a family name or epithet, so I kept it in the name. A rough calendar check: if 1747 is the expired year, Vaiśākha śukla 6 falls around 22–24 April 1825, which does not give a Monday. If 1747 is the current year (= 1746 expired), it falls around 3 May 1824, which is a Monday and matches 'saume'. So the date could be 1824 rather than 1825. This was checked only with mean new moons and is unconfirmed.
